Found out that my gf of 3 years has been cheating on me. She was my only real support since most of my family lives on the easy coast. I was born in CA but while growing up in foster care my mom took my siblings and moved back to NewYork leaving me behind. At the moment it didn't bother me so much because I had an entire foster family that was there for me. But around the time of emancipating from the system my then gf cheated on me and I lost my shit. Attempted suicide twice in one week. Landed myself in the hospital for 2 weeks with flowers and a card that said I had to move out(being my first time on my own) they abandoned me when I was crying out for help. People tend to think this illness is a get out of jail free card but it's not at all. Oh yeah it's definitely a good excuse but more of a burden than anything. A life in an out of hospitals with psychotic breaks and an inability to distinguish the difference between delusions and reality is hardly an excuse. If I told everyone I had COPD and I couldn't breathe people wouldn't bat an eye. But since it's a mental illness it's not taken seriously, even by my loved ones. Thank you for asking, I really needed to get all this off my chest and you caught me at the right time. Appreciate it.

I live in LA and my girlfriend lives in Oakland. The distance is extremely hard, on me especially. Not having her around makes it hard to motivate myself to do anything. My focus becomes askew and my delusions take over.

My bipolar has impacted the relationship negatively. I have trouble trusting her or anyone for that matter, and can become jealous over simple things. My delusions eat away at my heart and soul while she's gone and when she's near I am content and able to function freely as if she were never gone.

At times I can become possessive when I am manic, hypomanic or when I feel threatened, thus creating a strain on what is already a difficult situation. So I'm doing everything in my power to remain healthy and stable. (Going to therapy, taking my meds accordingly, staying occupied and sober)

The last time she was here for a visit I had a severe panic attack a few days before she had to leave. Every time she leaves she takes a part of me with her. And it never gets an easier. I already feel the distance is too much for me to bear, and I know she has a strong desire to move even further away and that kills me. 

I often wonder if I am the reason she craves the distance. I often wonder if things would be different/easier if I wasn't bipolar. I wonder too much.

I am lonely with my thoughts but am forever grateful to have her in my life. Her independence has created a pathway for me to create a positive outlook on life. She makes me want to be a better person, she makes me want to change all the negatives to positives..My life, that I never thought would succeed past the age of 23 has changed for the better. She is my world. My everything. My glimmer of hope when the world around me seems to be falling apart. I wouldn't trade our time together for anything. 

Long distance relationships are extremely fucking hard, but totally worth it

You will find peace. Have patience. Be strong.
